paragraphs.title: The Informer and His Harmful Tongue

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “Why boastest thou thyself in mischief?”
easy.q: What does the mighty man boast in?

easy.explanation: The tongue is compared to “a sharp rasor.”
The verse says the tongue is “working deceitfully.”

medium.explanation: The KJV says, “Thou lovest evil more than good.”
medium.q: What does the wicked man love more than good?

medium.explanation: He loves “lying rather than to speak righteousness.”
medium.q: What does he love instead of speaking righteousness?

medium.explanation: The verse calls them “all devouring words.”
medium.q: What kind of words does the deceitful tongue love?

answers: God’s goodness endures, while his mischief is condemned
Both are said to endure forever
challenge.explanation: God’s goodness “endureth continually,” while the man boasts in mischief.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between God’s goodness and the man’s mischief?

challenge.explanation: A sharp razor pictures speech that is cutting and deceitful.
challenge.q: What does the razor image suggest about the man’s tongue?

answers: The passage condemns boasting, lies, and harmful speech
The passage celebrates wealth and power
The passage teaches how to grow olive trees
challenge.explanation: These verses condemn the man’s evil boasting, lying, and destructive tongue.

easy.explanation: The verse says, “God shall likewise destroy thee for ever.”
easy.q: Who will destroy the wicked man?

easy.explanation: God will take him away and pluck him out of his dwelling place.
easy.q: What will God do to his dwelling place?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “The righteous also shall see, and fear.”

answers: Destroy, take away, and root out
medium.explanation: The passage describes destruction, removal, and being rooted out.
He will be rooted out “of the land of the living.”
medium.q: From what place will the wicked man be rooted out?

answers: They fear and laugh at him
medium.explanation: The righteous “shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him.”
medium.q: How do the righteous respond to his downfall?

answers: Complete removal and loss of life
challenge.explanation: The image indicates severe removal from life and community.
challenge.q: What does being rooted out of the land of the living suggest?

answers: Because they want to join him
challenge.explanation: Their fear reflects the seriousness of God’s judgment.
challenge.q: Why do the righteous fear when they see the wicked man’s punishment?

answers: A deceitful life leads to removal and destruction
challenge.explanation: The wicked man’s evil conduct is followed by divine destruction and removal.
challenge.q: What relationship does the passage show between wickedness and judgment?

paragraphs.title: Trust in Wealth versus Trust in God

easy.explanation: He “trusted in the abundance of his riches.”
easy.q: In what did the wicked man trust?

easy.explanation: He says, “I am like a green olive tree.”
easy.q: What kind of tree does the psalmist say he is like?

answers: In the land of the living
easy.explanation: The tree is “in the house of God.”
easy.q: Where is the green olive tree located?

answers: The wicked trusts riches, while the psalmist trusts God’s mercy
The wicked trusts God, while the psalmist trusts evil
medium.explanation: The verses contrast trust in riches with trust in God’s mercy.
medium.q: What is the main difference between the wicked man and the psalmist?

answers: He did not rely on God
medium.explanation: The phrase means that he did not make God his source of strength.
medium.q: What does the phrase “made not God his strength” mean?

answers: He trusts in the mercy of God
medium.explanation: The comparison follows his statement, “I trust in the mercy of God.”
medium.q: Why does the psalmist compare himself to a green olive tree?

answers: Life, flourishing, and security in God
Removal from the land of the living
challenge.explanation: The flourishing tree represents the psalmist’s secure trust in God.
challenge.q: What does the green olive tree symbolize in this passage?

answers: He depends on evil rather than God
He has abandoned all earthly possessions
challenge.explanation: He strengthens himself through wickedness instead of relying on God.
challenge.q: What does the wicked man’s self-strengthening in wickedness reveal?

answers: Trust in wealth differs greatly from trust in God’s mercy
All sources of trust have the same result
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the unstable trust of the wicked with faithful trust in God.
challenge.q: What principle is taught by the contrast in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Gratitude and Hope before God’s Faithful Ones

easy.explanation: He says, “I will praise thee for ever.”
The verse says, “I will praise thee for ever.”
easy.q: How long will the psalmist praise God?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will wait on thy name.”
easy.q: In what will the psalmist wait?

medium.explanation: The reason given is, “because thou hast done it.”
medium.q: Why will the psalmist praise God?

medium.explanation: The saints are God’s faithful and holy people.
medium.q: What does “thy saints” refer to in this verse?

medium.explanation: He promises to praise God and wait on His name.
medium.q: Which two responses does the psalmist express?

answers: It is offered only in trouble
challenge.q: What does “for ever” show about the psalmist’s praise?

answers: The psalmist praises God for His actions and continues trusting His name
The psalmist stops trusting after praising
The psalmist waits for earthly riches
challenge.explanation: Gratitude for what God has done is joined with continued trust in His name.
challenge.q: How are praise and waiting connected in this verse?

answers: The testimony is given in the presence of God’s faithful people
challenge.explanation: The phrase places the psalmist’s praise and hope before the faithful community.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “before thy saints” add to the meaning?
